subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should this issue be scoped to warning-only Control UI budget visibility first, or should save blocking and auto-archive be included in the same OpenClaw core change?
rationale: Current main already has partial diagnostics, while save refusal and archive behavior change user memory editing and recovery semantics beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Ship warning-only first
options.body: Add the Control UI MEMORY.md budget indicator and near-limit warning using existing bootstrap budget limits, leaving save blocking and archive behavior for follow-up decisions.

options.title: Block oversized saves
options.body: Make the Control UI or `agents.files.set` refuse saves over the configured bootstrap budget, but require an explicit override and recovery path.

options.title: Design archive workflow separately
options.body: Treat auto-archive as a memory persistence feature with pointer, undo, and doctor/recovery semantics before implementation.

recommendation.title: Ship warning-only first
recommendation.body: Add the Control UI MEMORY.md budget indicator and near-limit warning using existing bootstrap budget limits, leaving save blocking and archive behavior for follow-up decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history across the bootstrap warning implementation and the agent file/UI boundary touched by the requested warning surface.
